scheme_name: Assistance for Establishment of On farm Storage for Sorting-Grading
description:
The Assistance for Establishment of On-farm Storage for Sorting-Grading scheme was launched by the Government of India in 2018. 

This initiative is part of the broader efforts to enhance the agricultural sector and improve the income of farmers. 

The scheme aims to provide financial assistance to farmers for the establishment of on-farm storage facilities. 

The primary objective of the scheme is to reduce post-harvest losses by facilitating better storage practices. 

It also seeks to improve the quality of agricultural produce through sorting and grading. 

The scheme is designed to empower farmers by providing them with the necessary infrastructure to store their produce. 

The government has set a target to establish a significant number of on-farm storage facilities across the country. 

The assistance under this scheme is aimed at small and marginal farmers primarily. 

The financial assistance provided under the scheme is up to 50 percent of the total cost of the storage facility. 

For general category farmers, the maximum assistance limit is set at INR 25 lakh. 

For Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes farmers, the maximum assistance limit is increased to INR 30 lakh. 

The scheme covers various types of storage facilities including silos, warehouses, and cold storage units. 

Farmers can also receive assistance for sorting and grading equipment as part of the storage facility. 

The eligibility criteria for the scheme include being a small or marginal farmer. 

Farmers must possess land ownership documents to qualify for the assistance. 

The age limit for applicants is generally set at 18 years and above. 

There is no specific educational qualification required for this scheme. 

However, applicants must demonstrate a basic understanding of agricultural practices. 

The application process involves several steps that farmers need to follow. 

First, farmers must approach the local agricultural department or the relevant authority. 

They need to fill out the application form provided by the department. 

The application form requires details such as the farmer's name, address, and land ownership documents. 

Farmers must also provide a project report detailing the proposed storage facility. 

Once the application is submitted, it is reviewed by the concerned authorities. 

The authorities may conduct a field visit to assess the feasibility of the proposed project. 

After approval, the financial assistance is disbursed in installments. 

The first installment is usually released after the completion of the initial stages of construction. 

The second installment is released upon the completion of the storage facility. 

Farmers are required to maintain proper records of the expenditure incurred. 

The scheme is implemented by the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers' Welfare. 

State governments also play a crucial role in the implementation of the scheme. 

They are responsible for the disbursement of funds and monitoring the progress of the projects. 

Farmers can contact the local agricultural extension officer for more information about the scheme. 

The contact details of the agricultural department can typically be found on state government websites. 

The scheme is expected to significantly reduce post-harvest losses which are estimated to be around 15 to 20 percent in India. 

By improving storage facilities, farmers can store their produce for a longer duration. 

This allows them to sell their produce at better prices during off-seasons. 

The sorting and grading aspect of the scheme ensures that farmers can enhance the quality of their produce. 

Higher quality produce can fetch better market prices. 

The scheme also promotes the use of modern technologies in agriculture. 

Farmers are encouraged to adopt scientific methods for storage and preservation. 

The financial assistance provided under this scheme is part of the larger budget allocation for agricultural development. 

In the financial year 2021-2022, the government allocated INR 1,000 crore for various agricultural schemes including this one. 

The scheme is aligned with the government's vision of doubling farmers' income by 2022. 

It is also part of the larger framework of the Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samman Nidhi Yojana. 

Farmers can benefit from multiple schemes simultaneously to enhance their overall income. 

The scheme has been positively received by farmers across various states. 

Feedback from beneficiaries indicates an increase in income due to reduced wastage and better pricing. 

The government is continuously monitoring the implementation of the scheme. 

Regular assessments are conducted to evaluate the impact on farmers' livelihoods. 

The scheme is expected to evolve based on the feedback received from the ground level. 

Farmers are encouraged to participate actively in the scheme to maximize its benefits. 

The government also conducts awareness programs to educate farmers about the scheme. 

These programs are aimed at ensuring that farmers are well-informed about the application process. 

The overall goal of the scheme is to create a sustainable agricultural ecosystem. 

By providing financial assistance for storage, the government aims to empower farmers economically. 

The scheme is a significant step towards achieving food security in the country. 

It also contributes to the overall growth of the agricultural sector in India. 

Farmers are urged to take advantage of this scheme to improve their farming practices. 

The establishment of on-farm storage facilities is crucial for the future of agriculture in India. 

This scheme is a testament to the government's commitment to supporting farmers. 

It reflects the ongoing efforts to modernize agriculture and enhance productivity. 

Farmers are encouraged to stay updated on any changes or updates regarding the scheme. 

The government regularly publishes information on its official websites and through local agricultural offices. 

In conclusion, the Assistance for Establishment of On-farm Storage for Sorting-Grading scheme is a vital initiative for the agricultural sector. 

It provides essential financial support to farmers while promoting better storage practices. 

This scheme is a significant move towards reducing post-harvest losses and improving farmers' incomes.
